page: Amazon Web Services r8gn.2xlarge is an ARM-based memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and custom AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors. Operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz, the system provides 8 dedicated physical cores with single-threading, matching 8 virtual CPUs without hyperthreading contention. Cache configuration comprises 64 KB L1 data cache per core, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 64.0 GB, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Network connectivity features a 25 Gbps baseline bandwidth, while local disk storage is absent, requiring external Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional RAM subsystem throughput, highlighted by a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3212.87, placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 14.33 GB/sec, ranking in the top 25%. General computing and memory streaming perform consistently in the median tier, including stress-ng multi-core CPU output of 13641.63, Geekbench multi-core score of 9994.0, and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 153.96 GB/sec. In application-level benchmarks, the instance yields 17.78 million Redis SET operations per second and 19.31 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

Resource tradeoffs include the absence of onboard NVMe storage, meaning I/O profiles depend entirely on attached network storage. Additionally, CPU encryption testing in PassMark scored 1510.64 in the lower quartile, and LLM prompt processing on a 7B parameter model registered poor performance at 15.62 tokens/sec. The instance delivers favorable memory density per vCPU without hyperthreading overhead, making it well aligned for in-memory caching systems, distributed data analysis, Redis clusters, and mid-sized memory-bound transactional databases.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gn.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 8 dedicated AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 physical cores at 2.8 GHz and 64.0 GB of memory, yielding an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. Built on the AWS Nitro System, the instance incorporates 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without integrated local storage. Hardware benchmarking exhibits top-decile memory performance with a PassMark memory score of 3212.87 alongside strong single-thread bzip3 decompression of 14.33 GB/sec. General multi-core processing and Redis SET throughput remain solidly within median percentiles. Notable limitations include lower-quartile cryptographic performance and poor medium-model LLM inference throughput. Because storage must be provisioned externally over EBS, the platform provides strong resource efficiency for memory-heavy compute loads rather than local disk I/O, making it suitable for Redis caching, in-memory analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise database engines.
